title: Lead Compliance Risk Manager, Product Compliance - AI
description: About the role: As Mercury continues its rapid growth trajectory, navigating an increasingly complex regulatory, partner, and product landscape is critical. Compliance is not only a requirement, but a competitive advantage that enables Mercury to move faster, build trust, and launch innovative products responsibly.  Nowhere is that more true than in AI. We believe we have a path to lead the US banking* industry into the AI era, and that how we choose to build and deploy AI will define our success over the next three years.  We are building first-party agentic products, headless and agent-accessible banking through our API and MCP, and the internal platforms that let us build with AI at speed. Core to all of it is great governance—these systems must run on one trusted system of access, logging, and data controls that meets the requirements of our banking ambitions. We are seeking a Lead Compliance Risk Manager to serve as the compliance advisor for Mercury's AI products. This is a new, high-visibility role and the first dedicated compliance advisory seat covering AI at Mercury. You will be the leading authority on AI product compliance risk for the Compliance Team—shaping how we build, how we govern, and how we explain ourselves to our partners and regulators. You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Legal, and Operations to ensure Mercury's AI products are compliant-by-design from concept through launch and scale. You will also help define the AI governance framework itself: the standards, controls, escalation paths, and documentation that allow a bank-partnered fintech to deploy agentic capabilities responsibly and at pace. How this role fits alongside our other AI roles : this is a product compliance advisory role. Our Data & AI Governance team owns enterprise governance frameworks, responsible-AI standards, AI use case intake and inventory, and risk classification; Model Risk Management owns model inventory, tiering, and validation. You will be a close partner to and a major consumer of both—running our AI products through their processes, applying their standards to real product decisions, and bringing them the product-level detail they need to see. You will also help extend our existing product compliance playbooks to cover AI features, in partnership with your manager and the rest of the Product Compliance team. Your mandate is the products, not the program.  In this role, you will: Serve as the subject matter expert and primary compliance advisor for Mercury's AI and agentic products, including Command, our API, and agentic access methods such as MCP and CLI. Work closely with cross-functional risk and product teams to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a way that meets all relevant financial partner, regulatory compliance obligations, and our AI governance standards. Ensure all processes and products under your area of responsibility comply with applicable rules and regulations. Stay up to date with changes to applicable regulations, supervisory guidance, and emerging AI-specific law, and implement necessary updates to impacted products to maintain compliance. Support expansion for new product launches by scoping, defining, and communicating product and compliance requirements. Work cross-functionally to drive remediation efforts for products within your defined scope. Support the compliance function in defining and achieving departmental initiatives, maintaining relevant policies and procedures, developing documentation solutions, and liaising with auditors. Mentor and provide strategic guidance to compliance colleagues as AI capabilities spread across every product domain, and contribute to building a strong culture of compliance across Mercury. Work closely with our Risk team, which owns AI governance, as Compliance’s AI product expert to contribute product-level guidance to ongoing AI governance updates. Core responsibilities: Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Operations, and Legal to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a manner that meets all relevant regulatory, financial partner, and network obligations. Advise product and engineering teams throughout the product lifecycle—discovery, design, evaluation, launch, and iteration—to ensure AI products are compliant-by-design rather than reviewed after the fact. Identify, assess, and document compliance risks specific to AI and agentic systems—including inaccurate or fabricated output, unauthorized or over-scoped agent action, inadequate consent and disclosure, unexplainable decisioning, disparate impact, data leakage across customers or organizations, prompt injection and third-party agent risk, and insufficient audit trail—and work cross-functionally to design pragmatic mitigation strategies. Define the compliance requirements for the platforms AI is built on, in partnership with the teams that own them: the LLM gateway all internal traffic routes through, the internal app

We believe that ensuring data is trusted shouldn’t slow teams down—it should accelerate what’s possible. This led us to develop the first technology platform for responsible data use in 2016. Today, with AI representing the latest and most impactful expansion of data yet, OneTrust is once again redefining what responsible innovation looks like. OneTrust, the AI‑Ready Governance Platform™, unifies regulatory intelligence, automation, and connected governance workflows so businesses can continue to move at the speed of AI while ensuring good governance to prevent data misuse at scale. Trusted by thousands of organizations worldwide, OneTrust is shaping the future where trusted data becomes a transformative force for business and society.   The Challenge We are seeking a highly motivated and Senior Manager of Corporate Accounting to help drive the next phase of our accounting organization’s evolution. This role sits at the intersection of accounting, controls, and business transformation. The ideal candidate combines deep accounting expertise with operational leadership capabilities and a passion for process improvement. This individual will help establish a scalable controls environment, lead reporting initiatives, and assist in developing the company's AI governance and controls framework. Your Mission Internal Controls & Risk Management Design, implement, and continuously improve a scalable internal controls framework across accounting and finance processes. Partner with process owners to identify control gaps, evaluate risks, and implement sustainable remediation plans. Support SOX readiness, compliance programs, and internal audit activities. Develop control documentation, narratives, risk assessments, and testing methodologies. Establish governance processes around emerging technologies, including AI-enabled solutions. Monitor evolving accounting standards and assess organizational impact. Systems Implementation & Process Improvement Support finance transformation initiatives, including ERP, reporting, consolidation, and workflow automation projects. Serve as a key accounting stakeholder during system implementations and enhancements. Evaluate existing processes and recommend automation opportunities. Develop scalable accounting workflows that improve efficiency while maintaining control integrity. Assist in roadmap planning for finance technology investments. Data Integrity & Governance Partner with Finance Systems, Business Systems, and Data teams to improve master data quality and governance. Support initiatives focused on financial data accuracy, completeness, and consistency. Develop monitoring processes and controls around critical financial datasets. Assist in root-cause analysis and remediation of data quality issues impacting financial reporting. AI Governance & Controls Framework Assist in establishing an AI Controls Center of Excellence within the finance organization. Develop policies, standards, and governance frameworks for AI-enabled accounting and finance processes. Design controls around AI-generated outputs, model monitoring, data integrity, and regulatory compliance. Partner with Information Security, Internal Audit, Legal, and Business Systems to develop an enterprise AI control environment. Evaluate opportunities to responsibly leverage AI to improve accounting operations and decision-making. You Are/Have Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance. CPA required. 8+ years of progressive accounting, audit, financial reporting, or finance transformation experience. Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP, technical accounting, and financial reporting requirements. Experience designing and implementing internal controls. Experience supporting M&A integrations and carve-outs. Experience with system implementations and finance transformation initiatives. Knowledge of SOX 404, COSO, and internal audit methodologies. title: Manager, Account Management
description: Who are we? At UpGuard , we are replacing manual security bottlenecks with AI-driven precision. Fresh off a US$75M Series C, we are scaling our infrastructure to process 100 billion risk signals daily. This isn’t just growth; it’s a total reimagining of how the world manages cyber risk. We build the Cyber Risk Posture Management (CRPM) platform that security teams actually love. By integrating security ratings, threat intel, and agentic AI, we empower organisations to stay ahead of an ever evolving attack surface. We aren’t just building another tool; we’re defining a category. We provide the autonomy to ship world-class technology and the resources to do it at a global scale. Where does this role fit in? We are looking for a dynamic, self-motivated, and ambitious strategic thinker with a successful track record to join our leadership team as a Manager of Account Management. This position will report to the Head of Customer Success, Americas. Our Account Management team is focused on driving revenue retention and expansion through renewals, cross-sells, and upsells for our highest-touch customers. We work closely with Sales, Marketing, and Product to ensure customer satisfaction and long-term success. What will you do? Build and lead a team of Account Managers focused on managing renewals, cross-sells, and upsells for high-touch customers Scale, mentor, and develop a high-performing Account Management team Accurately forecast monthly and quarterly revenue retention and expansion results Drive strategy and build executive relationships for top accounts Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams (Sales, Marketing, Product) to optimize results and customer engagement Use data and metrics to assess team performance and implement improvement initiatives Ensure adherence to UpGuard’s post-sale processes and standards Foster a culture of accountability and customer-first thinking within the team Build close alignment with team leaders and individual contributors to support mentorship and career growth for high-performers Develop and execute customer retention strategies, ensuring high customer satisfaction and long-term account stability. What will you bring? A minimum of 2 years of leadership experience managing Account Managers or similar post-sales teams, with a proven track record in revenue retention and expansion At least 3 years of experience in B2B SaaS as an individual contributor, ideally with a focus on renewals, cross-sells, upsells, and a proven track record Experience in leveraging post-sales technology stacks such as Hubspot (CRM) and Gong (Revenue Intelligence) to coach and guide your team Demonstrated ability to plan, monitor, and optimize post-sale activities based on team performance and customer feedback A problem-solver who simplifies complex challenges and fosters collaboration across teams Leadership with an executive presence, capable of influencing at all levels A customer-centric mindset, passionate about building and nurturing long-term relationships A goal-oriented, collaborative approach that thrives on teamwork and diverse perspectives What will give you an edge? title: Third-Party Security Risk Management (TPRM) Lead
description: Your work days are brighter here. We’re obsessed with making hard work pay off, for our people, our customers, and the world around us. As a Fortune 500 company and a leading AI platform for managing people, money, and agents, we’re shaping the future of work so teams can reach their potential and focus on what matters most. The minute you join, you’ll feel it. Not just in the products we build, but in how we show up for each other. Our culture is rooted in integrity, empathy, and shared enthusiasm. We’re in this together, tackling big challenges with bold ideas and genuine care. We look for curious minds and courageous collaborators who bring sun-drenched optimism and drive. Whether you're building smarter solutions, supporting customers, or creating a space where everyone belongs, you’ll do meaningful work with Workmates who’ve got your back. In return, we’ll give you the trust to take risks, the tools to grow, the skills to develop and the support of a company invested in you for the long haul. So, if you want to inspire a brighter work day for everyone, including yourself, you’ve found a match in Workday, and we hope to be a match for you too. About the Team The Cybersecurity Risk team is responsible for cybersecurity risk assessments, security exception management, TPRM, and partner eco-system security. This broader team is responsible for technology governance, compliance, and risk programs. About the Role As a Third-Party Security Risk Management (TPRM) Lead on the Cybersecurity Risk team, you will own and evolve our Cybersecurity third-party risk management (TPRM) program while also leading principal-level risk assessment activities across the broader risk portfolio. You will partner with business units and stakeholders including Security, Cloud Operations, IT, Development, Infrastructure, Procurement, Legal, and Compliance to identify and assess security issues and gaps, communicate risk and business impact to leadership, and drive remediation actions and timelines to closure. This is a strategic yet hands-on role that combines program ownership, cross-functional influence, and deep risk expertise. Responsibilities:- Third-Party Risk Program Ownership: Own and evolve the Cybersecurity third-party security risk strategy, including risk assessment methodology, vendor tiering, control expectations, procedures, continuous monitoring, and reporting; mature the program to keep pace with emerging risk domains such as AI/ML vendors and evolving regulatory expectations. Third-Party Risk Assessments: Lead risk assessments for critical and operationally significant third parties (partners, vendors), identifying, tracking, and due diligence, ongoing monitoring, issue management, and exit. Broader Risk Assessment and Analysis: Perform principal-level risk assessment activities beyond third parties — including security exception management, internal control reviews, and cyber risk assessments — applying qualitative and quantitative techniques to translate risk into business impact and inform risk-based decisions. Stakeholder Engagement and Escalation: Partner with Legal, Procurement, Privacy, ERM and business owners to ensure risks are appropriately documented, accepted, mitigated, or escalated; communicate complex vendor and risk landscapes and prioritization decisions clearly to senior leadership. Metrics and Reporting: Establish and maintain key risk and performance metrics, dashboards, and Outcome-Driven Metrics (ODMs) that demonstrate program progress, maturity, and effectiveness, and continuously refine initiatives based on data-driven insights and stakeholder feedback. Automation and Innovation: Drive automation of high-volume, repetitive processes and evaluate AI-enabled tooling to increase efficiency, quality, and speed while scaling the program responsibly. Leadership and Continuous Improvement: Lead large-scale, cross-functional initiatives to mature TPRM and risk capabilities, coach and develop team members, contribute to the evolution of risk and program best practices, and support other risk, governance, and program activities as needed. About You Basic Qualifications 12+ years experience in GRC, leading GRC initiatives, developing and maintaining GRC frameworks, and ensuring organizational compliance with applicable laws and regulations. 7+ years of experience implementing and managing modern GRC tools (e.g., ServiceNow GRC, OneTrust, Archer, LogicGate) to automate evidence collection and continuous control monitoring. B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Information Security, Management Information Systems (MIS), or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Other Qualifications Expert-level understanding of Third-Party Risk Management across the full third-party lifecycle — intake, due diligence, vendor tiering, ongoing monitoring, issue remediation, exception and risk acceptance, and exit planning — and the proven ability to define, lead, and mature enterprise-wide TPRM program
